A sophisticated freeway network extends throughout the Los Angeles area, and both the Los Angeles Harbor and Long Beach areas are linked to the main part of Los Angeles by several expressways / The Harbor Freeway (Calif. Hwy 11), the Long Beach Freeway (Calif. Hwy 7), and Interstate Highway 4057. Consequently, the east-west line dividing the Los Angeles Harbor zone and the Los Angeles commercial zone is hereby abolished, and the geographic limits of the Los Angeles commercial zone shall be determined by reference to the population-mileage formula adopted in this proceeding. Motor carrier and freight forwarder terminal areas at Los Angeles shall also be determined by the population-mileage formula.
A few brief comments with respect to the construction of operating rights are warranted. Those carriers holding certificates or permits designating service at Los Angeles whether stated as "Los Angeles, Calif." or the "Los Angeles commercial zone" or the "Los Angeles zone" - shall be deemed to hold authority to serve Los Angeles and all points within 20 miles of the Los Angeles corporate limits. From this time on no distinction shall be made between Los Angeles and the Los Angeles Harbor zone, and we will only issue certificates and permits phrased in terms of service at Los Angeles. Many outstanding certificates and permits, however, do designate service at the "Los Angeles Harbor zone" or the "Los Angeles Harbor" or "Los Angeles Harbor points."
